toegepas.blok: Sê waar een plek teenoor 'n ander lê
toegepas.voor: en lê dus wes van die huis
toegepas.rede_vinder: Avoids repeating 'van die huis' twice in one sentence and matches the parallel 'noord daarvan' in the next sentence.
toegepas.fout: 'van die huis' is repeated twice in one sentence, which reads stiffly beside the parallel 'noord daarvan' in the next sentence.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'daarvan' can only point to the house, so the repetition goes and the two sentences match without the meaning moving.

toegepas.blok: Die son wys die rigtings buite
toegepas.voor: sak teen die einde van die dag in die weste
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Saans' is the natural counterpart of 'soggens' earlier in the sentence and replaces a wordy phrase without changing the meaning.
toegepas.fout: 'teen die einde van die dag' is a wordy, loose phrase where Afrikaans has a plain time word to pair with 'soggens'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'saans' is the natural counterpart of 'soggens', reads more simply for Grade 4, and keeps the same time and direction.

laat_vaar.voor: Albei lees jy van die kaart self af
laat_vaar.na: Jy lees albei van die kaart self af
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Fronting 'Albei' with inversion reads stiffly for Grade 4; subject-first order is more natural and keeps the meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Fronting 'Albei' with inversion is natural Afrikaans that ties back to the two items just named, so the reordering is a lateral move.

vlae.teks: Albei lees jy van die kaart self af.
vlae.rede: 'Albei' follows sentences about the key and the compass rose, but the block also introduced the north arrow, so a learner may read 'albei' as the compass rose and north arrow; clarifying the reference would mean guessing the intended content, so it is flagged rather than changed.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Die son wys die rigtings buite
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: om buite rigtings te vind sonder enige kaart
laat_vaar_vorige.na: om buite sonder 'n kaart rigtings te vind
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'sonder enige kaart' after the verb copies English 'without any map'; Afrikaans places the 'sonder' phrase before the object and uses ''n'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Lateral move: putting the 'sonder' phrase after the verb is natural Afrikaans, and 'enige' carries the deliberate emphasis of no map at all, which the proposal weakens.
